transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have the six-week cell-phone pilot proposal to review today, covering grades 9 and 10 with open classroom bins and a tentative launch of September 2, 2026. Before I make any decisions on final scope, procedures, or the launch record, I'd like to hear from our participating teacher, our counselor, and our technology coordinator. Who would like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to share what I found in my classroom trial. Across all my 9th-grade sections, I recorded 23 phone-related interruptions in just two weeks. However, when I tested numbered locking pouches, they significantly reduced interruptions. Based on that, I recommended a grade-9-only pilot using one pouch per student in my team notes — but those notes haven't been added to the draft proposal yet.

transcript.text: Before we finalize procedures, I need to flag a critical safety exception. Two students have active safety plans requiring them to receive time-sensitive messages from their caregivers during the school day. I confirmed these plans with both families this week, but the exception has not yet been entered into the pilot procedure. We need to build in a mechanism for these students before any approval.

The student-information system's phone-registration module will not be ready until September 16, 2026, and our technology change plan requires the pilot to launch with a digital registration record on that date. I confirmed the deployment date with the district systems team this week, but the draft proposal still shows September 2 as the tentative launch. We cannot launch on September 2 without the registration module in place.
